L61: Rating: ⭐⭐⭐
L62: 
L63: Visited: 03/23/2018 | Recommended: ✅ Yes
L64: What They Liked Most:
L65: I have very mixed feelings for this attraction. Although it was the off-season, I may have expected too much from this haunt as I thought it would be ... more similar to The Darkness when it comes to scares that come at you 360. This is a totally different haunt and it is probably a lot creepier on a dark, fall night. There was only one line entertainer but he was doing a great job of scaring haunted house owners and staff before they entered.
L66: It was interesting to see that they had some complications with their ticketing system and the VIP ticket line or path was very unorganized. We could hear staff on the radios basically saying they didn't know what to do with people and that they didn't realize VIP needed to go first.
L67: The general admission line we were waiting in allowed no room or reserved space for VIP holders so they literally had to squeeze their way to the front of the line past all the rest of us with no one to lead the way for them (parts of the line went upstairs and it was pretty dark). We may have seen a staff member with a flashlight lead them to the front twice.
L68: This is a professional attraction and this wasn't it's first rodeo so I'm really hoping it isn't that disorganized during Sep/Oct when there are a lot more ppl in line. I think my favorite part was what we experienced leading to the show. The outside of the building is authentic and creepy. The queue line weaves you past an old elevator and other features of the brewery. There is a large spiral staircase that takes you to the basement and this was awesome.
L69: There were some well-decorated scenes but for the most part it was very hard to focus on the details and there was so much fog that sometimes we wouldn't realize there was an actor in the room with us until we were on our way out. Most of the acting crew just stood and stared at us as we walked past them and a few lunged at us or yelled 'grr' 'rawr' etc which is about the same thing that they did at Darkness last time we visited.
L70: Some of their costumes were obviously cheaper, store-bought and we weren't expecting that at all from an attraction ran by other, large houses that are high quality. There was a long and pretty plain maze that was rather difficult but it was boring as well. Other groups were demanding the actors to tell them how to get out because it wasn't fun, it was aggravating. It seemed like it was a way to stretch out the length of the haunt or take up space without really trying.
L71: When we heard sounds some of it was random hard rock music and while that helped us get in a head-banging mood, it didn't intensify the creepy factor other than how loud it was when we were closer to the speakers because it didn't allow us to hear anything else. All in all, we are glad we went because we had never been here before but I don't think I will go back. Not unless I hear a lot has changed and a lot of people raving about it.
L72: I put that I would recommend it to friends bc I would recommend going at least once so you can say you did and check out the creepy building.Read More

by Mansfield News JournalSeptember 19, 2026

SHELBY — Jake and Jessica Rietschlin have carved out their own niche in the competitive field of Halloween attractions.

This year marks the 10-year anniversary of one of two attractions at the family farm, 5482 Ohio 61, near the Shelby Settlement, an unincorporated rural community located southwest of Shelby and southeast of Crestline.

“When our kids were younger, we went to all the different corn mazes and pumpkin patches,” Jessica said. “We thought it would be fun to do one here.”

Each year, the maze features a theme. The Rietschlins started with “Peanuts” character Charlie Brown.

L47: ## Worlds of Fun Code of Conduct
L48: 
L49: Worlds of Fun is committed to Protecting the Fun by providing a safe, comfortable, and enjoyable experience for all guests. To help us fulfill our commitment, we ask that you honor this Code of Conduct.
L50: 
L51: ### On Halloween Haunt operating days, the following policies apply:
L52: ### Halloween Haunt Chaperone Policy
L53: 
L54: This policy will be in effect from open to close on all Halloween Haunt operating days.
L55:   * All guests age 17 years old or younger must be accompanied by a chaperone who is at least 21 years old to be admitted to or remain in the park.
L56:   * The policy will be in effect during all operating hours, on HAUNT operating days.
L57:   * The chaperone must present a valid government-issued photo identification with date of birth upon entry.
L58:   * One (1) chaperone may accompany no more than Five (5) guests age 17 or younger per day.
L59:   * In addition, the chaperone must accompany their party during entry and remain with the party for the duration of their stay.
L60:   * Guests 18 years of age or older may be asked to present a valid government-issued photo identification (Driver's license, State Issued ID Card, Passport) with date of birth at entry to verify their age. If unable to verify proof of age, guests may be denied entry into the park.
L61:   * Guests age 17 years old or younger who are found inside the park unaccompanied by a chaperone when the Chaperone Policy is in effect will be subject to ejection.
L62:   * This chaperone requirement applies to all Worlds of Fun ticket and season passholders.
L63: ### Halloween Haunt Bag & Liquids Policy
L64: 
L65:   * After 6:00 PM, all bags must be no larger than 12” x 12” x 6”, regardless of material (clear or opaque).
L66:   * Each guest is permitted to bring only one bag into the park after 6:00 PM.
L67:   * All bags are subject to x-ray inspection and search before entry.
L68:   * This policy applies to all bag types, including backpacks, purses, diaper bags, and camera bags.
L69:   * Liquid bottles, thermoses or cups must be empty upon arrival.
L70: ### Halloween Haunt Code of Conduct
L71: 
L72: The following behaviors are not permitted at Worlds of Fun:
L73:   * Carrying firearms, ammunition, knives, self-defense or restraining devices (e.g., pepper spray, mace) and weapons of any kind and any other prohibited item. Worlds of Fun reserves the right to prohibit any items at their discretion
L74:   * Fireworks or other similarly explosive and/or flammable objects
L75:   * Unsolicited photography or video recording that disrupts a guest’s experience or interferes with park operations
L76:   * Unruly or disruptive behavior that interferes with guests’ enjoyment of the park including running, the incitement of running, and blocking midways and exits
L77:   * Fighting or physical aggression of any kind, including verbal and physical assaults
L78:   * Acts or behavior that park management determines is a safety concern or that interrupts park operations or guests’ experience
L79:   * Harassing/threatening behavior, sexual misconduct or lewd behavior including inappropriate interaction with park guests or associates
L80:   * Offensive language or gestures
L81:   * Clothing with offensive language, obscene gestures/graphics, or nudity or clothing that does not sufficiently cover undergarments. Face coverings that conceal identity. (This policy does not apply to masks meant to reduce the spread of Covid-19 and other germs.)
L82:   * Intoxication or substance impairment that results in irresponsible behavior
L83:   * Smoking/Vaping is only permitted in designated smoking areas
L84:   * Entering restricted areas including but not limited to ride Danger Zones and behind-the-scenes areas
L85:   * Line Breaking- includes leaving and re-entering a line for any reason or place holding in line
L86:   * Theft of any kind
L87:   * Selling park tickets or soliciting and distributing literature not sponsored by the park
L88:   * Refusing to follow verbal or printed instructions or to cooperate with park personnel or security
L89:   * Liquid bottles, thermoses or cups must be empty upon arrival
L90: ### Halloween Haunt Themed Attire and Face Make Up Policy
L91: Family-oriented themed outfits/attire are permitted. Attire must not represent or resemble any official Park character, disrupt regular company operations, or potentially harm another guest or associate. Attire and accessories must meet Code of Conduct dress requirements and may not be offensive or violent and may not disrupt the general safety of guests or associates. Guests wearing character themed outfits may not sign autographs for other guests or represent themselves as a park associate.
L92: Costumes that conceal identity are prohibited. Rides and attractions may also have additional restrictions on dress attire.
L93: During HAUNT operations, guests age 12 and older are prohibited from wearing costumes, face paint, masks, or anything that conceals identity or causes confusion in identifying professional scare actors.
L94: ### Halloween Haunt Re-Entry Policy
L95: 
L96: No Re-Entry will be allowed beginning at 6:00 PM, nightly, during HAUNT operations.

L143: ### Please also note the following:
L144: ### Children/Teens - Notice to Parents & Guardians
L145: Parents or guardians are responsible for the behavior of their minor children. Appropriate behavior and supervision are the responsibility of the parent/guardian and is always expected. In addition to our chaperone policy, we strongly recommend that minors (under 18) be accompanied by an adult. The park does not assume any responsibility or liability for unattended minors. Parents/guardians may be held legally liable for all acts of the children under their care.
L146: ### Personal Conduct
L147: 
L148: Conduct deemed by Worlds of Fun to be inappropriate for the peace and good order of the park, guests, or associates, and which may adversely affect the safety of others is not permitted. Anyone who violates the Code of Conduct may be subject to ejection without refund.
L149: 
L150: Guests are encouraged to report any violations of the Guest Code of Conduct or suspicious activity to the nearest Worlds of Fun associate, Security associate, or to call (816) 303-5090.
L151: Worlds of Fun reserves the right to revise or modify this Code of Conduct with or without notice.
L152: 
L153: Notice: Worlds of Fun Security personnel utilize surveillance cameras and body worn cameras as part of their overall security program.
L154: #### Why are you implementing this policy?
L155: 
L156: A safe, family-friendly atmosphere of Worlds of Fun is the type of experience our guests expect and deserve. In recent years, there have been increasing incidents of unruly and inappropriate behavior across our industry and at other major entertainment venues. This policy is being put in place to ensure that all guests have the best time ever and leave happy and eager to visit again.
L157: #### I’m coming with a pre-scheduled company event or school group, does this policy apply?
L158: 
L159: A chaperone policy still applies to prescheduled company events and school groups. If you purchased tickets through our Group Sales department and have questions, please contact your Group Sales representative.
L160: #### Does the chaperone need to always stay with the group?
L161: 
L162: Chaperones must accompany their party during entry, remain inside the park during their visit, and be available by phone throughout their stay.
L163: 
L164: One (1) chaperone may accompany no more than six (6) guests ages 16 or younger per day.
L165: #### What happens if guests 16 years old or younger do not have a chaperone?
L166:

Accessibility may vary by attraction area, event, operating configuration, and safety conditions.

Guests who may require an accommodation are encouraged to contact us before visiting. Advance notice gives our team the best opportunity to discuss available options and determine how we can assist without compromising guest or employee safety.

## mobility access

Some areas may involve uneven surfaces, narrow passages, thresholds, ramps, or route limitations.

Please contact us before your visit if you use a wheelchair, walker, mobility aid, or have difficulty navigating extended walking routes. We can provide current information about accessible entry, routes, and any operational limitations.

Staff members cannot lift or carry guests or mobility devices.

## sensory considerations

The attraction is intentionally designed to create an intense sensory experience. It may not be appropriate for every guest.

Visitors who are sensitive to flashing lights, loud sounds, fog, darkness, enclosed spaces, sudden contact, disturbing imagery, or other theatrical effects should review our Safety Disclaimer and contact us with questions before purchasing admission.

Reasonable accommodation requests will be considered individually. Because certain effects and environmental conditions are fundamental to the haunted-attraction experience, not every effect can necessarily be removed or avoided.

## service animals

Trained service animals may accompany guests in public areas as permitted by applicable law.

However, the attraction includes darkness, loud noises, sudden effects, performers, crowds, fog, and other conditions that may frighten, distract, or endanger an animal.

Please contact us before visiting with a service animal so we can discuss the attraction environment, current route conditions, and available options.

Emotional-support, comfort, and therapy animals that are not trained to perform a task for a person with a disability may not qualify as service animals under applicable law.

## companions and support persons

Guests who require assistance may attend with a companion or support person, subject to applicable admission requirements.

Please contact us in advance if you have questions about admission or accommodations for a required support person.

## effective communication

Guests who need information in an alternative format or require communication assistance should contact us. We will make reasonable efforts to provide information in an accessible format or identify another effective method of communication.

## requesting an accommodation

To request an accommodation or ask an accessibility question, contact us before your visit whenever possible.

Please include:

  * The date you plan to attend
  * The accommodation or information requested
  * The best way to contact you

You do not need to provide unnecessary private medical details. We may ask limited questions when needed to understand the requested accommodation and applicable safety considerations.

## feedback

We welcome feedback about website or attraction accessibility. If you experience a barrier, please tell us:

  * The page, feature, or attraction area involved
  * The problem you experienced
  * The device, browser, or assistive technology used, if relevant
  * How we can contact you about the issue

We will review accessibility feedback and make reasonable efforts to address confirmed barriers.

# Tarantula’s Haunted Grotto

By

Anthony Mariani

- 

October 29, 2025

0

Facebook Twitter

Image: bttiki10-29-e1761777394430-681x624Tarantula Tiki Lounge’s Halloween cocktail menu will be available thru Fri. 

Tarantula Tiki Lounge (@Tarantula_Tiki) is going all out this Halloween. The retro-fabulous SoMa cocktail retreat is throwing one of the biggest parties of its kind in town 6pm Fri. With a vendor market and live music, Haunted Grotto Under the Sea offers a lot for a little: Admission to the 21-and-up shindig is free.

“We feel like our vibe is a little like Halloween all year round,” said Tarantula owner Autumn Brackeen, “so what better place to throw a holiday bash?”

Haunted Grotto will be Tarantula’s second Halloween concert/market. Last year’s was so popular, “we decided to make it an annual thing,” Brackeen said.

Image: MUL_FIFA_ZERO_Digital_300x250

Dallas’ “Satanic” metalheads Daughters of Evil, garage rockers Prof. Fuzz 63, and exotica lovers the S.S. Castaways will perform starting at 7pm, and the vendors will include food pop-up Swizzle.

Courtesy of Planteray, Tarantula Tiki Lounge will feature the rum in such drinks as the Mai Time to Die, Ghoul Summer, and Creature Feature.

Haunted Grotto Under the Sea will take place inside the Tarantula and outside in the loading area of the nearby W.A. Powers building and the MicroPark alleyway. The outdoor bar will serve beer and THC beverages in addition to the signature Planteray Halloween cocktails.

“There’s nothing like Halloween with a tiki vibe,” Brackeen said, “and no one can catch that Halloween magic quite like we can.”

> ##### Haunted Grotto Under the Sea

> ##### 6pm Fri w/Daughters of Evil, Prof. Fuzz 63, the S.S. Castaways, and vendors at Tarantula Tiki Lounge, 117 S Main St, Fort Worth. Free. 21+.

【turn37search4】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 4 months ago; Crawled: 2 weeks ago; Content type: text/html; Field of Screams Branson at Ballparks of America runs 18 nights from Oct. 2 to Oct. 31, 2026, plus four November crossover nights. Hours and attractions.
Branson, MO — Field of Screams Nixa is opening a new indoor haunted attraction inside Ballparks of America in Branson on Sept. 11. The new operation, Field of Screams Branson, will run roughly 40,000 square feet at launch under a multi-year sublease from Ballparks of America, with a plan to grow to 100,000 square feet over the next few years.

The Branson site is the company’s first indoor attraction. The outdoor Field of Screams Nixa haunt, the operator’s main attraction at 2142 N Sports Complex Lane in Nixa, will continue to run in the fall.

## About Field of Screams Branson

The Branson location will occupy the former Red Roof Mall building inside the Ballparks of America campus. The launch attraction is called the 9th Inning Nightmare, a nod to the baseball venue. Owner Derrick Moore told OzarksFirst.com that the sets will be on a cinematic scale to match the larger-than-life vibe of Branson’s other attractions.

Moore said he will also be running new entertainment attractions owned by Ballparks of America, including zombie laser tag, glow mini golf, and escape rooms. The 270,000-square-foot Ballparks of America campus will continue to operate normally, including its fall baseball-tournament schedule, with the haunt sharing the property.

## Field of Screams Nixa Remains Open

The Branson expansion is in addition to, not in place of, the existing outdoor haunt. The operator told supporters on the company’s official Facebook page that “Field of Screams Nixa is NOT going anywhere” and that the original Nixa haunt is returning for the 2026 season with “new scares, new experiences, and even more nightmares.” Guests can attend either or both locations; the company described them as “two completely different experiences.”

## Event dates and ticketing

Field of Screams Branson opens Sept. 11 and runs through the end of October. The schedule is Fridays and Saturdays in September, then Thursdays through Sundays in October. Moore told OzarksFirst.com that a Christmas-Halloween crossover event is also planned later in the year. Ticket pricing has not yet been announced; ticket giveaways and sneak peeks are coming via the new social channels.

For more information, visit the Field of Screams Branson page or the operator’s Nixa website.

## The Beginning – Curse of The Hollows

Darkness falls on the small town of Hollow Point. Ranchers, hunters, and townsfolk once thrived here—until the curse took root. Some say it began with the Vulture Witch, feathers black as night. Others say it was vengeance for blood spilled on sacred ground. Whatever the truth, souls now twist into shadows, and those who linger too long are never the same.

Image: The Hollows at Brookdale Farms in Eureka, MO - Haunted Trail Near St. Louis

## The Saloon of the Damned

## Once filled with music and laughter, the Hollow Point saloon never found peace. The piano plays itself, mirrors reflect faces that aren’t your own, and the Belle of the Hollows still smiles at strangers—though if she takes your hand, you’ll never leave.

Image: The Hollows at Brookdale Farms in Eureka, MO - Haunted Trail Near St. Louis

## The Gallows Grove – Hollow Marshal on Horseback

## The sheriff’s rope could not cleanse the curse. Thirteen souls swung beneath the crooked tree, but now the Hollow Marshal rides eternally on his skeletal steed. His noose swings, his eyes burn, and when you hear the creak of rope behind you—do not look back.

Image: The Hollows at Brookdale Farms in Eureka, MO - Haunted Trail Near St. Louis

## The Twisted Trailhead – The Vulture Witch

## What was once a safe road for ranchers now crawls with cursed roots and whispering trees. The Vulture Witch waits in the branches above. If you hear her voice, it’s already too late.

## The Ghostly Fiddler

## The fiddler of Hollow Point played at every gathering—until the skinwalkers came. Now his mournful tune drifts on the wind, luring travelers closer. Beware: when the music stops, the silence is worse than death.

## The Cornfield Rider

## Beyond the corn rows rides the headless Rider of the Hollows. His axe gleams with lightning, his steed breathes smoke and fire, and the ground trembles at his charge. If his shadow crosses you, another neck will roll before dawn.

Image: The Hollows at Brookdale Farms in Eureka, MO - Haunted Trail Near St. Louis

## The Trapper’s Camp

## The Haunted Barn – Burned Rancher

This barn once sheltered cattle and grain, the pride of a rancher’s work. But fire swept through, leaving only ash. Now, the Burned Rancher walks these ruins. His skin smolders, his hat fused to his skull, his voice forever begging for water. The hay hides more than vermin — it hides the things he calls his own. If the flames don’t claim you…he will.

L284: ## The Beginning – Curse of The Hollows
L285: 
L286: Darkness falls on the small town of Hollow Point. Ranchers, hunters, and townsfolk once thrived here—until the curse took root. Some say it began with the Vulture Witch, feathers black as night. Others say it was vengeance for blood spilled on sacred ground. Whatever the truth, souls now twist into shadows, and those who linger too long are never the same.
L287: 
L288: 【52†Image: The Hollows at Brookdale Farms in Eureka, MO - Haunted Trail Near St. Louis†static.wixstatic.com】
L289: ## The Saloon of the Damned
L290: 
L291: ## Once filled with music and laughter, the Hollow Point saloon never found peace. The piano plays itself, mirrors reflect faces that aren’t your own, and the Belle of the Hollows still smiles at strangers—though if she takes your hand, you’ll never leave.
L292: 
L293: 【53†Image: The Hollows at Brookdale Farms in Eureka, MO - Haunted Trail Near St. Louis†static.wixstatic.com】
L294: 
L295: ## The Gallows Grove – Hollow Marshal on Horseback
L296: ## The sheriff’s rope could not cleanse the curse. Thirteen souls swung beneath the crooked tree, but now the Hollow Marshal rides eternally on his skeletal steed. His noose swings, his eyes burn, and when you hear the creak of rope behind you—do not look back.
L297: 
L298: 【54†Image: The Hollows at Brookdale Farms in Eureka, MO - Haunted Trail Near St. Louis†static.wixstatic.com】
L299: 
L300: ## The Twisted Trailhead – The Vulture Witch
L301: ## What was once a safe road for ranchers now crawls with cursed roots and whispering trees. The Vulture Witch waits in the branches above. If you hear her voice, it’s already too late.
L302: 
L303: ## The Ghostly Fiddler
L304: 
L305: ## The fiddler of Hollow Point played at every gathering—until the skinwalkers came. Now his mournful tune drifts on the wind, luring travelers closer. Beware: when the music stops, the silence is worse than death.
L306: 
L307: ## The Cornfield Rider
L308: ## Beyond the corn rows rides the headless Rider of the Hollows. His axe gleams with lightning, his steed breathes smoke and fire, and the ground trembles at his charge. If his shadow crosses you, another neck will roll before dawn.
L309:

L311: 
L312: ## The Trapper’s Camp
L313: ## The old trapper knew these woods, but the skinwalkers flayed him like the hides he once tanned. His broken form begs for help beside the campfire, but step too close and you’ll be dragged into his fate.
L314: ## The Haunted Barn – Burned Rancher
L315: 
L316: This barn once sheltered cattle and grain, the pride of a rancher’s work. But fire swept through, leaving only ash. Now, the Burned Rancher walks these ruins. His skin smolders, his hat fused to his skull, his voice forever begging for water. The hay hides more than vermin — it hides the things he calls his own. If the flames don’t claim you…he will.

L327: ## The Hollows FAQs
L328: ### What is The Hollows Haunted Trail?
L329: 
L330: The Hollows Haunted Trail is an outdoor haunted walkthrough experience at Brookdale Farms near St. Louis, MO. Guests traverse fog-filled woods, corn-maze sections and themed scenes pulled from Old West legends, featuring live actors, strobe lights and immersive effects.
L331: 
L332: ### How long does the trail last?
L333: 
L334: The estimated duration to complete The Hollows is about 40 minutes, though actual time may vary depending on pace.
L335: ### How much are tickets and what is included?
L336: 
L337: General admission for the 2025 season is listed as $28 (including tax and service fees) for one person. There is also a “Bundle Pass (4 Guests)” available online for $100. Tickets include admission to The Hollows haunted walkthrough only. Prices are subject to change.
L338: ### Is this attraction suitable for children or all ages?
L339: 
L340: Yes — the attraction is open to “All-Ages.” However, anyone under 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Brookdale Farms asks that parents use their discretion with young children. Be aware: it’s a haunted trail with live actors, fog, strobe lights, and scary scenes.
L341: ### What type of scares and effects are present?
L342: 
L343: The trail features outdoor scare-elements including fog, strobe lights, live actors, and thematic scenes (woods, corn maze, etc.). This is a full immersive haunt experience—not a mild walk-through.
L344: ### Are there age, mobility or health restrictions I should know about?
L345: 
L346: While there is no explicit minimum age listed, because of the nature of the attraction (darkness, sudden scares, uneven terrain such as woods and a corn maze), guests with mobility issues, photosensitivity (from strobe lights), or who are easily startled should consider whether the experience is appropriate for them or their children. (Brookdale Farms asks parents to use their own discretion for younger children.)
L347: ### How do I purchase tickets and is it better to buy ahead?
L348: 
L349: Tickets can be purchased online. A 4-Guest bundle pass is available online only. Pre-purchase is recommended because the ticket sales end one hour before closing, and you must check in by that time. Arriving late may risk not being allowed to join the trail.
L350: ### What else is available on site (food, drink, other activities)?
L351: 
L352: On-site beverage purchases are available at the “Sippin’ Saloon”. Brookdale Farms also has other attractions and events on select nights at the same time as The Hollows that will require a separate ticket purchase.
L353: ### What should I wear?
L354: 
L355: Wear comfortable shoes and dress for outdoor terrain and weather (trail goes through woods and corn maze). Avoid wearing costumes that could get caught or restrict movement. Since fog, strobe lights and live actors are involved, consider comfort and safety (e.g., if sensitive to strobes or loud noises). Bring a light jacket if evenings are cool.
L356: ### Are refund or reschedule options available?
L357: 
L358: No refunds or transfers unless the attraction is closed due to weather.
